title: Modular curves, following Katz–Mazur, Part II: Uniformization, integral boundary and Hecke cohomology
summary: A complete target-level planning pass for generic-fibre compatibility, bad reduction and geometric Hecke cohomology through finite Taylor–Wiles control. All 75 required targets already have canonical accepted nodes in the R13.3 and R14.3 packets. This packet imports them without creating duplicate nodes, synchronizes the reader with the corrected statements and reconciles the cross-part dependency contracts. All nine stages are planned, with nine explicit gaps and the supplier requests retained. No stage is claimed closed or implemented.

requests.need: Refined Γ₀(n) compactification of Česnavičius Theorem 5.13, using decontractions and compatibility of cyclic subgroups, as well as honest Γ(n), fixed-pairing and Γ₁(n) stacks. In particular distinguish the regular DM refined stack from the naive Artin Γ₀ stack; their coarse spaces agree, not their stacks. Additional consuming contract: Actual smooth fine elliptic family, compactification, universal elliptic curve on its open locus, and good reduction over Z[1/N]. For Theorem 5.16 additionally supply the ordinary dense locus, the connected–étale decomposition of E[p], and lifting of its order-p subgroups after finite extension. R14.1 supplies the integral correspondence and its specialization.

Import the prime N≥5 diamond quotient cusp package over ℤ[1/N]: Tate torsion/level covers, integral closures, cusp labels, widths, characteristic-2/3 ramification and stabilizers; establish identity-compatible agreement rather than rebuilding it.

Coherent restriction, flat base change and dualizing sheaves for proper flat nodal curves; torsion-free sections are determined on a schematically dense locus, including the formal-completion restriction when each component meets the boundary. Additional consuming contract: Integrate the general finite-coefficient étale–Betti comparison with locally constant coefficients, compact support, traces and cup products required by accepted RS-06 as UPSTREAM:CohomologicalPointCounting:ComplexComparison:etale-Betti. Also supply finite-generation/Mittag–Leffler inverse-limit exactness and comparison to the pinned pro-étale EllAdicCohomology carrier. The checkout has no resolvable roadmap anchor for that RS-06 upstream label; do not substitute de Rham comparison.
Elliptic quotients by finite locally free subgroup schemes, the universal quotient isogeny and its degree; no new elliptic-curve or quotient carrier is defined here.
Relative Weil pairing on elliptic torsion, alternating perfection and compatibility with an isogeny, including the multiplier equal to its degree.

Algebraic/analytic component identification of the already constructed coarse curves, including determinant orbits, cusp fields and honest full-level versus scalar-framed conventions. Additional consuming contract: Actual cusp fields and a Q-rational cusp on the chosen X₁(N) model; distinguish 0 on the (E,P) model from infinity on X₀(N).
Canonical algebraic/analytic compactification comparison with its cusp parameters, descent maps and weight-two normalization; use R13.4a as its algebraic input, never the aggregate R13.4.

The universal ordinary elliptic deformation with Serre–Tate parameter and the supersingular one-dimensional deformation, including Frobenius/Verschiebung torsion and Drinfeld-generator conditions. The exact current ModularCurves Layer 7F–7H and Layer 8C outputs are imported, not re-planned.

Import the existing elliptic PD-3 target: relative Frobenius and Verschiebung in characteristic p with V∘F=[p]=F∘V, together with the PD-1 finite locally free torsion levels and Cartier duality from Layer 2E. For a regular local ring finite over its invariant subring, a finite residue-trivial group of order invertible in the residue field has regular invariants exactly when its cotangent image is generated by pseudo-reflections. This is an additional supplier contract requested from the quotient owner, not an assertion that its current R09.5 packet already has a pseudo-reflection node. Current ModularCurves 9C supplies only its more restricted Katz–Mazur quotient criteria.

Existing arithmetic-surface blowups, total transforms, exceptional self-intersection, contractions of admissible −1 curves, regular resolutions and compatibility with flat base change. This part adds only the modular input rings and stabilizer actions.

gaps.title: Wild coarse bad-level interior models at 2 and 3
gaps.detail: The required arbitrary-N Γ₀(pⁿM) component/multiplicity target and R20 cases include p=2,3. Edixhoven’s exact interior invariant-ring/minimal-resolution formulas are proved for p>3. Česnavičius gives all-prime coarse cusp regularity and regularity away from exceptional interior j-values, not the missing wild local equations. Required calculation: use imported cyclic deformation rings, compute the actual finite stabilizer action at level-dividing 2 or 3 (including infinitesimal inertia), identify normal invariant completions and their multiplicities, resolve and export branch/thickness maps. A tame order-2/3 eigencharacter argument is insufficient. The fine rigidified one-p-factor uv=p model is separated from this coarse descent gap.

gaps.title: Relative curve norm and principal polarization contract
gaps.detail: JacobianChallenge D proves the field curve Jacobian. A0-extension supplies relative Picard space, lifting and a neutral-component criterion; it does not by itself supply the curve-specific relative canonical principal polarization/norm theorem over ℤ[1/N]. The request to A0-extension and AbelianSchemes A2 names this exact additional comparison. No fictional relative Jacobian carrier or field-only-to-relative inference is made.

gaps.title: Integral cuspidal-symbol realization contract
gaps.detail: Current ModularForms Layer 8 constructs the full Γ₁-coinvariant module Div⁰(P¹(ℚ))⊗Sym and a Hecke-equivariant period quotient onto the form-side image. It explicitly does not require an isomorphism of its whole module with S_k⊕conj(S_k); boundary/Eisenstein classes and integral torsion must be handled. The local R14.2 comparison target must construct the weight-two cuspidal boundary kernel modulo torsion and identify its integral Hecke action with compact-curve H₁, or the appropriately transposed dual H¹, retaining all diamond and bad-prime conventions. Determine exact kernels at the integral level, rather than inferring them from rational dimensions or period injectivity on forms. The J/Betti/Tate comparison remains separate and justified.

gaps.title: Integral higher-weight boundary and lattice range
gaps.detail: Deligne supplies rational Sym^r cohomology. Prove the exact good-prime Hecke eigensystems on H⁰ and cusp inertia cohomology for Sym^r integral coefficients; specify residual ideals where they vanish and where reduction and saturated parabolic comparison hold. For ℓ≤r symmetrization need not be perfect: choose a divided-power/dual lattice with a sourced comparison or retain a weaker pairing. The present conditional theorem does not claim unconditional integral freeness or perfectness in that range. The symbol comparison must identify the standard representation with the dual geometric relative-H¹ coefficient system, including determinant twists, and prove the Manin/geodesic relative-chain presentation on B. Deligne and the rational even-weight boundary model do not by themselves establish this integral identification.

gaps.title: Deep input to the S-arithmetic congruence kernel theorem
gaps.detail: Serre 1970 §2.6 gives the correct real-place specialization, but its proof depends on central Mennicke-symbol/congruence-kernel calculations and the Moore/class-field-theory input. Those intermediate theorems have not been decomposed against the baseline. A follow-up must supply that exact proof chain; an unrelated profinite arithmetic action theorem cannot replace it.

gaps.title: Tree fundamental edge and enhanced congruence-character proof
gaps.detail: Refine the principal-level fundamental-edge argument and CDT Corollary 4.5.3 conjugation-invariance criterion against existing finite-group and approximation APIs. The source statements and the target proof routes are read, but the strong-approximation/reduction-surjectivity and finite congruence quotient sublemmas are not yet supplier-closed. This is a proof-chain gap, not permission to erase the congruence subspace from ordinary Ihara. For congruence-invariance, supply the exact continuous-cohomology, Künneth and Hochschild–Serre proof interfaces, Lazard’s uniform-group calculation, adjoint-cohomology vanishing, and a reproducible proof of the level-8/16 computations used in CDT §4.5.11. These source inputs are not declarations established by the pinned ordinary H¹ carrier.

gaps.title: Integral modular old/new and quaternionic pivot exactness
gaps.detail: Ribet–Stein §3.10.2 equation (3.2), p. 48 involves a quaternionic Shimura-curve Jacobian J′_{pq}(K). The exact sequence 0→X_p(J′_{pq}(K))→X_q(J(K,pq))→X_q(J(K,q))²→0 needs the specific Cerednik–Drinfeld identification and integral Hecke-compatible maps. Generic Néron functoriality and a rational old/new isogeny do not establish this integral sequence. Keep the conditional torus theorem here; arrange a lower-tier geometric interface before the higher Hilbert/Shimura-curve roadmap consumes it, or explicitly narrow the requested consumer. Retain finite cokernels and component groups until that proof is supplied.

gaps.title: Extensions of the exact Ihara consumer range
gaps.detail: The compact constant-coefficient Γ₁(N) result includes ℓ|N on characteristic-zero curves and has no exceptional residual-image hypothesis. It does not by itself prove level lowering, nor a uniform Sym^r/coarse Γ₀(N) or characteristic-ℓ fibre result. R20/R22 must use the stated fine/mixed-level weight-two prefix, or specify a sourced further injectivity theorem with its stabilizer, coefficient and exceptional-image hypotheses; Γ₀(N) has a Shimura-subgroup kernel.
